flags: Public Storage closed its acquisition of National Storage Affiliates Trust (NSA).
Public Storage completed its acquisition of PS Canada.
In its third quarter release, Public Storage raised its 2026 guidance for Same Store NOI and Core FFO per share.
no_value_reason: no valuation route yet for a real estate company or trust

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description.
business_model.claim: Public Storage sells month-to-month self-storage space, for personal and business use, in 3,171 consolidated facilities with 229 million net rentable square feet. These are the largest self-storage portfolio in the U.S. and operate under the Public Storage name.
quotes: which offer storage spaces for lease on a month-to-month basis, for personal and business use

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q income statement line items.
business_model.claim: The income statement splits revenue into self-storage facilities and ancillary operations. In Q3 2026, total revenues were 1,366,190 (table in thousands): self-storage 1,254,111 and ancillary 112,079 (both table in thousands). Self-storage is the large majority.

Ancillary activities are tenant reinsurance, third-party facility management, merchandise sales (locks and boxes) and bridge loans to third-party owners. Third-party management covered 362 facilities, and the bridge loan receivable was $142.1 million at year-end 2025.
quotes: We implemented a lending program in 2024, under which we provide bridge lending financing to third-party self-storage owners for operating properties that we manage.

business_model.claim: Same-store revenue moves with occupancy and realized rent per occupied square foot. In 2025, rent per occupied square foot rose 0.5% to $22.54, offset by a 0.4% fall in average occupancy to 92.0%, so revenue was roughly flat.
quotes: due primarily to a 0.5% increase in realized annual rent per occupied square foot partially offset by a 0.4% decrease in average occupancy

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: In 2026, same-store rent per occupied square foot was up 0.2% in Q3 but down 0.3% over nine months, while average occupancy was up 0.3% and 0.2% respectively. Same-store revenue was up 0.5% in Q3 and flat over nine months.
quotes: Realized annual rent per occupied square foot for our Same Store Facilities increased by 0.2% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and decreased by 0.3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and Part II risk factors.
business_model.claim: Revenue growth now depends heavily on acquired and newly developed facilities. Since the beginning of 2024, the company has expanded by 881 facilities and 63.3 million net rentable square feet for $11.6 billion. This includes the NSA acquisition and the PS Canada acquisition.
quotes: we have expanded our portfolio by a total of 881 facilities with 63.3 million net rentable square feet for a cost of $11.6 billion
On July 22, 2026, we closed the acquisition of National Storage Affiliates Trust (“NSA”).

business_model.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and balance sheet.
business_model.claim: Growth has been funded with cash and debt. Nine-month cash disbursed for acquisitions was 1,862,709 versus 814,555 a year earlier (both table in thousands). Net real estate facilities were 25,126,038 versus 18,804,558 at year-end 2025 (both table in thousands).

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A same-store table and text.
business_model.claim: Same-store operating costs are led by property taxes. In 2025, direct cost of operations was 820,373 (table in thousands), of which property taxes were 378,266 (table in thousands). Cost growth that year came from property taxes and indirect costs, partly offset by lower marketing and on-site payroll.
quotes: due primarily to increased property tax expense and indirect cost of operation partially offset by decreased marketing expenses and on-site property manager payroll expense

business_model.claim: Customer acquisition relies on Google search, which makes marketing spend a cost driver and a dependency. More than half of new storage customers in 2025 came through Google search.
quotes: More than half of our new storage customers in 2025 were sourced directly or indirectly through “unpaid” search and “paid” search campaigns on Google.

business_model.claim: Acquisition activity raised depreciation, interest and one-time costs. In Q3 2026, revenue rose but operating income fell to 316,960 from 491,517 (both table in thousands). Depreciation and amortization was 412,614 versus 290,364, and transaction and integration expense was 114,642 versus 0 (all table in thousands).

business_model.basis: Stated in the income statement and earnings release table.
business_model.claim: Debt financing cost is a growing expense. Q3 2026 interest expense was 102,534 versus 79,692 (both table in thousands). The weighted average interest rate on debt was 3.6% versus 3.0%.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 and the 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Earnings also move with foreign currency and the Shurgard stake. The company holds 35% of Shurgard, a European self-storage operator. Nine-month 2026 net income benefited from a foreign currency gain, tied mainly to euro-denominated notes payable.
quotes: a $282.6 million increase in foreign currency gain primarily associated with our euro-denominated notes payable

business_model.basis: Stated in the earnings release guidance table.
business_model.claim: Management raised 2026 same-store guidance in the Q3 release. Same-store revenue growth is guided at —% to 0.5% and Core FFO per share at $16.90 to $17.10. This is management's stated outlook, not an independent forecast.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 as management belief.
competitive_position.claim: Public Storage describes itself as the largest US self-storage owner. It holds about 9% of US self-storage square footage, the four largest owners together hold about 22%, and the remaining 78% sits with regional and local operators.
quotes: We are the largest owner of self-storage facilities in the United States (“U.S.”), with physical presence in most major markets and 40 states.

As the largest owner of self-storage facilities, we believe that we own approximately 9% of the self-storage square footage in the U.S. and that collectively the four largest self-storage owners in the U.S. own approximately 22%, with the remaining 78% owned by regional and local operators.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: The portfolio grew sharply in 2026 through acquisitions. Since the start of 2024 it added 881 facilities with 63.3 million net rentable square feet for $11.6 billion. The NSA and PS Canada deals closed in Q3 2026 and added over 1,100 stores.
quotes: Since the beginning of 2024, including the ongoing integration of unstabilized properties acquired prior to 2024, we have expanded our portfolio by a total of 881 facilities with 63.3 million net rentable square feet for a cost of $11.6 billion.
adding over 1,100 stores to the PS Next™ operating platform

competitive_position.claim: The balance sheet grew with the acquisitions. Total assets were 28,997,613 at Sep. 30, 2026 versus 20,208,604 at Dec. 31, 2025, with goodwill and other intangibles rising to 1,355,953 from 251,613 (table in thousands).

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the quote is management's characterization.
competitive_position.claim: Same-store operations were roughly stable in Q3 2026. Revenue rose 0.5%, average occupancy was 92.2% versus 91.9%, and management cites improving churn, occupancy and move-in trends.
quotes: We continue to post encouraging trends on churn, occupancy, and move-in rates, which drove positive Same Store revenue, NOI and Core FFO per share growth

competitive_position.claim: Pricing power was weak in 2025. Demand softness forced lower move-in rates for new tenants. Same Store average occupancy fell to 92.0% from 92.4%, and revenue was essentially unchanged.
quotes: Softness in demand for our storage space has led to lower move-in rental rates for new tenants and lower average occupancy in 2025 as compared to 2024.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Technology and the digital channel are cited as advantages. Nearly three quarters of new rental agreements in 2025 were completed through eRental and Rent by Phone. The same dependence on Google is flagged as a risk.
quotes: Nearly three quarters of our new rental agreements were completed by customers using our eRental® and Rent by Phone process during 2025.
More than half of our new storage customers in 2025 were sourced directly or indirectly through “unpaid” search and “paid” search campaigns on Google.

competitive_position.claim: The 10-K names competition as a threat. Competition from other operators, developers and storage alternatives could hurt occupancy, rates and advertising costs, and more capital or development could add supply.
quotes: Significant competition from self-storage operators, property developers, and other storage alternatives may adversely impact our ability to attract and retain customers and may negatively impact our ability to generate revenue.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q risk factors, plus the income statement figure.
competitive_position.claim: Acquisition integration is a named threat to the position. The 10-Q warns that NSA and PS Canada synergies may not be realized on time, and Q3 transaction and integration expense was 114,642 (table in thousands).
quotes: We may be unable to successfully integrate the operations of NSA and PS Canada with ours and may not realize the anticipated synergies and other benefits of the transactions or do so within the anticipated time frame.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release and balance sheet.
competitive_position.claim: Financial strength supports the position, but leverage and funding costs have risen. Credit ratings are A2 / A, net debt to EBITDA is 3.4x versus 3.0x, and the weighted average interest rate is 3.6% versus 3.0%.
Higher interest rates are a named threat to the growth plan. They raise the cost of capital used to underwrite acquisitions and development.
quotes: Increases in our cost of capital impact our assessment of the yields we consider appropriate to support pursuing property acquisition and development opportunities and thus can impact our external growth prospects.

competitive_position.claim: Regulation can constrain pricing. California and other jurisdictions have limited rents, fees, marketing and other practices, and the company says that losing its pricing methodology could significantly hurt results.
quotes: California and other jurisdictions have also adopted regulations restricting our operations relating to pricing methodologies, restrictions on fees, procedures for selling stored property of delinquent tenants, marketing restrictions related to price changes and promotional rates, zoning restrictions and other matters.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the income statement and the 10-K.
competitive_position.claim: Ancillary lines add some diversification. Ancillary revenue was 112,079 in Q3 2026 versus 85,206 (table in thousands). The company also runs bridge lending and holds a 35% stake in Shurgard.
quotes: We hold a 35% interest in Shurgard Self Storage Limited (“Shurgard”).

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 8-K and the 10-K risk factors.
competitive_position.claim: Leadership change is a named execution risk. The 10-K flagged recent changes in Chairman, CEO and CFO, and on November 11, 2026 the President, Chief Digital & Transformation Officer agreed to leave effective January 31, 2027.
quotes: agreed that Ms. Johnson will leave the Company, effective January 31, 2027

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release guidance table.
competitive_position.claim: Management raised 2026 guidance in the Q3 release. Core FFO per share is now $16.90 to $17.10 versus a prior $16.75 to $17.05, and same-store NOI growth is (0.8)% to 0.2%, up from (2.0)% to (0.3)%.

financial_health.claim: Cash and equivalents were 560,379 (table in thousands) at the latest quarter-end, up from 318,095 at year-end. The unsecured credit facility and commercial paper line, undrawn at year-end (0), carried 200,000 (table in thousands).
quotes: Unsecured credit facility and commercial paper | 200,000 | 0

financial_health.basis: Ratings from the earnings release table; program size from the 8-K. Using both as support for market access is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The company reports credit ratings of A2 / A (Moody's / S&P), unchanged year on year, and has a commercial paper program of $1.0 billion. These support its access to debt markets.

Forward sale agreements under the ATM program cover 1,230,141 common shares, with expected net proceeds of approximately $399.2 million if physically settled. This is a contingent equity funding source.
quotes: we had outstanding forward sale agreements under our ATM program for a total of 1,230,141 common shares

financial_health.basis: Balance sheet figures are stated. The link to acquisitions is inferred from the acquisition activity in the cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Debt on the balance sheet rose. Notes payable were 11,992,033 (table in thousands) against 10,253,881 at year-end. Total liabilities were 13,777,654 against 10,866,770, and total equity was 15,219,959 against 9,341,834, so equity grew by more than liabilities.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release table. The mechanism is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Leverage ratios rose and coverage fell versus a year earlier. Net debt to EBITDA was 3.4x against 3.0x, net debt and preferred equity to EBITDA was 4.7x against 4.2x, and EBITDA to fixed charges was 6.3x against 6.8x. The weighted average interest rate was 3.6% against 3.0%.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the income statement and cash flow statement. The cause is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The interest burden is rising. Interest expense for the nine months was 267,333 (table in thousands) against 223,310. For the quarter it was 102,534 against 79,692.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement. The explanation is inferred from its line items.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow for the nine months was 2,272,091 (table in thousands), lower than 2,452,862 a year earlier, even though net income was higher.
quotes: Net cash flows from operating activities | 2,272,091 | 2,452,862

financial_health.basis: Stated in the statements. The link to euro-denominated notes is stated in the 10-Q MD&A item, which also reports a larger foreign currency gain for this period.
financial_health.claim: Net income of 1,410,661 (table in thousands) was helped by a foreign currency exchange gain of 68,728, against a loss of (213,866) a year earlier. This gain is largely non-cash, since the cash flow statement removes an unrealized foreign currency gain of (70,970). Reported earnings are therefore a weaker guide to cash than the operating cash flow line.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release reconciliation. Both are non-GAAP measures defined by the company.
financial_health.claim: On the company's own cash-flow-style measures, results are broadly flat. Core FFO per share was $12.74 against $12.71 for the nine months. FAD was 2,085,512 (table in thousands) against 2,125,120, a decline of (1.9)%.

financial_health.basis: Cash flow figures are stated. The funding interpretation is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Investing outflow of (2,527,510) (table in thousands) exceeded operating cash flow of 2,272,091. The gap was covered by net financing inflow of 497,703, including notes payable issuance of 1,658,770, a term loan of 500,000 and commercial paper of 200,000, partly offset by repayments of (683,895). Acquisitions used (1,862,709) in cash.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated. The timing explanation is inferred from the balance sheet and the supplemental non-cash schedule.
financial_health.claim: Distributions paid fell to (1,186,292) (table in thousands) from (1,727,546), but this reflects timing. Dividends and distributions payable at period end were 583,263, against 1,898 at year-end, so operating cash flow comfortably exceeding distributions paid overstates the cushion.

financial_health.basis: Use of proceeds is stated in the 8-K. The issuance completion is stated in a later 8-K. The comparison of coupons is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Near-term debt maturity: the company plans to use net proceeds from its new $500 million 5.600% senior notes to repay commercial paper and then to partially repay at maturity the $650 million 1.500% Senior Notes due 2026. The new notes were completed and mature in 2036.
quotes: The Company expects to use the net proceeds to repay amounts outstanding under PSOC’s $1.0 billion commercial paper program and to use the remaining net proceeds to partially repay at maturity the outstanding $650 million in aggregate principal amount of PSOC’s 1.500% Senior Notes due 2026.

financial_health.basis: Issuance details are stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The average maturity figures are from the earnings release table.
financial_health.claim: The company has recently extended and diversified its debt. It issued $900 million of senior notes in July with net proceeds of $886 million, and C$400 million of 4.540% notes due in 2033 in September. Weighted average years to maturity were 6.1 against 6.4 a year earlier.
The note indenture requires the issuer to maintain total unencumbered assets of at least 125% of total unsecured indebtedness. This is a covenant constraint on further unsecured borrowing.
quotes: the Indenture requires PSOC to maintain total unencumbered assets of at least 125% of total unsecured indebtedness

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and cash flow statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Acquisitions are the main growth driver. Since the beginning of 2024 the portfolio has grown by 881 facilities and 63.3 million net rentable square feet, at a cost of $11.6 billion. Cash disbursed for acquisitions in the nine months was 1,862,709 (table in thousands).
quotes: we have expanded our portfolio by a total of 881 facilities with 63.3 million net rentable square feet for a cost of $11.6 billion.

growth_thesis.basis: Risk language is stated in the 10-Q; the link to the departure is inferred from the 8-K.
growth_thesis.claim: Condition: the NSA and PS Canada acquisitions, which added over 1,100 stores, must be integrated successfully and deliver the expected synergies. Management itself lists integration failure as a risk.
quotes: We may be unable to successfully integrate the operations of NSA and PS Canada with ours and may not realize the anticipated synergies and other benefits of the transactions or do so within the anticipated time frame.
Closed the acquisitions of National Storage Affiliates and Public Storage Canada, adding over 1,100 stores

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the counter is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Non-same-store NOI is the clearest earnings contributor. Combined NOI from Acquired and Developed and Expanded Facilities rose 95.6% ($73.3 million) in the quarter and 52.0% ($107.6 million) over nine months.
quotes: combined net operating income generated by our Acquired Facilities and Developed and Expanded Facilities increased 95.6% ($73.3 million) and 52.0% ($107.6 million), respectively

growth_thesis.basis: Figures and management commentary are stated in the earnings release; the conditions are inferred.

Annual contract rent per occupied square foot at quarter end was up 1.2%. For this to continue, move-in rates, churn and occupancy must keep improving.
quotes: We continue to post encouraging trends on churn, occupancy, and move-in rates

growth_thesis.claim: Management raised 2026 guidance. Same Store NOI growth is now guided to (0.8)% to 0.2%, and Core FFO per share to $16.90 to $17.10. Delivery depends on the rest of the year tracking the year-to-date trends.
quotes: Increased outlook for the full-year 2026, including Same Store NOI by 90bps and Core FFO per share by $0.10

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and 10-K; the spending comparison is read from the cash flow statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Development and expansion is a secondary driver. Developed and Expanded Facilities number 121 with 14.0 million net rentable square feet, at a completed cost of $1.8 billion. Management says it will increase development only when yields exceed those of acquisitions.
quotes: For development and expansions completed by September 30, 2026, we incurred a total cost of $1.8 billion.
We plan to increase our development activity when we identify attractive risk adjusted return profiles with yields above those of acquisitions.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated; the link to portfolio growth is stated in the 10-K and inferred for the 2026 rise.
growth_thesis.claim: Ancillary operations are growing. Q3 ancillary revenue was 112,079 against 85,206 a year earlier (table in thousands), and ancillary NOI rose by $19.6 million. For this to continue, the tenant reinsurance and related businesses must grow with the portfolio.
quotes: a $19.6 million increase in ancillary net operating income
as we grow our self-storage portfolio through acquisition, development and third-party management, we have the opportunity to increase the growth profile of our tenant reinsurance business.

growth_thesis.basis: Metrics are stated in the 10-Q and earnings release; the conditional link is stated in the 10-K risk factor.
growth_thesis.claim: Condition: external growth needs continued access to capital at a workable cost. Net Debt to EBITDA was 3.4x against 3.0x, and the weighted average interest rate was 3.6% against 3.0%. Forward ATM sales represent expected net proceeds of about $399.2 million, and a $900 million senior note offering was completed.
quotes: Increases in our cost of capital impact our assessment of the yields we consider appropriate to support pursuing property acquisition and development opportunities and thus can impact our external growth prospects.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated; the dilution reading is inferred.
